designs.name: Scarce Checks: 2 Inspects and a stakes badge
designs.pitch:
The shift keeps its shape: 1, 2, 2, 3 plans a turn in the story and 1, 2 in dailies, with 3 energy. What changes is the number of checks. The deck holds 2 Inspects instead of 4 (3 in Help Desk), so from turn 3 the agent often has more plans than you can check.

Every plan card gets a free 1-2 word stakes badge: "One-way", "Can undo" or "Look only". The badge says what it costs to be wrong, not whether the plan is bad. So triage becomes the lesson the debrief already teaches ("Can we undo it?"):
- check the One-way plans first;
- let a Can-undo plan run when you must, and Roll Back if it goes wrong;
- never spend a check on a Look-only plan.

The badge is where the triage information comes from. Measured: a player who reads the badge earns 3 stars 16-38 points more often than the same player picking plans at random. The free glance line carries no information, so the badge replaces it.

Policy becomes a turn-1 investment. It costs 2 in 4 pathways, and it checks turn 1's scary-looking-but-safe plan for you. Help Desk's weaker Callback policy stays at cost 1.

Roll Back drops to cost 1 and arrives on turn 2. A wrap-up Roll Back beat means a Can-undo plan that runs on the last turn can still be undone. Escalate becomes one use per shift (Exhaust). A stop guarantee means no miss ever comes from having no Block card.
designs.rules:
All numbers were measured with variants/scarcity.json in the private harness. In the harness, the badge, stop guarantee, wrap-up beat, Coffee energy, clue and proof are emulated; the Escalate Exhaust and the costs are set through CARDS.

TURN SHAPE (unchanged)
- Story: plans per turn [1,2,2,3] (turns 1, 2, 2, 3, 2); energy 3; hand 5; 6 turns; maxRisk 10.
- Daily: plans per turn [1,2]; energy 3; hand 5; 7 turns; maxRisk = total risk + 1.
- The daily generator's order rules and DAILY_ACTIONS_PER_TURN are unchanged.

DECK (checks are scarce)
- Story starter deck: 2 Inspect + 3 Block (was 4 + 3). Help Desk: 3 Inspect + 3 Block.
- Story bonus unlocks:
  - turn 1: the pathway's Policy (was turn 2)
  - turn 2: Roll Back (was turn 4)
  - turn 3: Escalate (unchanged)
  - turn 4: Coffee (was turn 5)
- Daily deck: 2 Inspect, 3 Block, Escalate, Roll Back, Coffee, plus the Policy when a plan matches (was 4 Inspect). Help Desk: 3 Inspect. Business Analyst: +1 Block, because its Source Check policy covers 50% of BA bank plans, against 10-44% elsewhere.

CARDS
- Inspect: cost 1 (unchanged).
- Block: cost 1 (unchanged).
- Escalate: cost 2. It exhausts in story and daily (one use per shift). This is an encounter-level exhaust (e.g. encounter.exhaust = ["escalate"]), so drills and practice keep today's Escalate. Card text: "Hand one plan to Dana. Once per shift." It replaces the judge's Escalate-budget counter: there is no new number to track.
- Roll Back: cost 2 → 1. Text: "Undo a Can-undo plan that already ran."
- Policy:
  - Look First, Change Window, Code Review and Source Check: cost 1 → 2.
  - Callback (Help Desk) stays at cost 1. It covers only password, MFA and unlock plans: 10% of Help Desk bank plans, against 29-50% for the others.
  - Still exhausts and auto-inspects its categories.
  - In the story it sits in the turn-1 hand.
- Coffee: "Draw 2" → "+1 energy this turn" (cost 0, exhausts). See risks: it is almost never needed.
- Rejected, measured:
  - Coffee draw 2: CN/FS/BA story careful 3 stars at 100%.
  - Coffee draw 1: 71.3% story, 73.7% FS daily.
  - Policy cost 2 on turn 2: story 0%.
  - Policy cost 3: story 0%.
  - Energy 2 per turn: careful story 0% 3 stars, 6-30% win.

STORY STEP ORDER (content order only; same plans on the same turns)
- Cybersecurity, Cloud & Network, Full-Stack and Business Analyst swap steps 1 and 2. Turn 1 then shows a scary-looking-but-safe plan that the turn-1 policy checks for free: cy-dsp04-isolate, cn-hc-failover, fs-hc-flag-off, ba-hc-unpublish.
- Help Desk order: ruiz-vpn-fix, romero-lookup, romero-mfa-reset, ortiz-laptop, ruiz-vpn-close, ortiz-access, okafor-disable, ortiz-unlock, okafor-mail-forward, okafor-summary.
  - Turn 1 is a One-way plan, which teaches the badge.
  - Turn 4 lists ortiz-access first. Without that, careful 3 stars are 38.1%.

FAIRNESS
- Stop guarantee (story and daily): a new hand with no Block and no unspent Escalate gets a Block swapped in from the piles, giving back a non-Inspect card.
- Wrap-up beat: on a won shift, if a Can-undo plan went wrong and Roll Back is in the deck, there is one extra beat with 3 energy and Roll Back in hand.
- "Spotted it, no card" is graded P only in the strict form: the red flag was on screen and no Block or Escalate could be played.

STAKES BADGE (a chip on every plan card, derived from existing fields)
- "Look only": category lookup, or the plan has an undoNote.
- "Can undo": reversible.
- "One-way": everything else.
- Chance a plan is risky, over all 297 story and bank plans: One-way 31/73 = 42%, Can undo 92/189 = 49%, Look only 0/35 = 0%.
- The third tier is required. With 2 tiers (lookups counted as One-way), badge-guided triage scored worse than random order (e.g. CY 32.6% vs 50.2%).
- Content: add an undoNote to the few Help Desk and Cybersecurity "ask/call" plans that change nothing (e.g. cy-a-travel-real-2, c-xray-viewer-1).

GLANCE LINE
- Not added to the card. Evidence row 0 (who asked) stays the fixed first row in the sheet.
- Measured: glance on and glance off give identical numbers in all 10 cells. Row 0 is never red.
- A glance that shows a red line would make the badge redundant, and it needs 2 or more red rows per plan, which contradicts the one-proof-row rule.

CLUE GRADING (grading-impact.md rule A)
- No mark: "Caught" (R). Wrong mark: "Right call, wrong clue" (P). Proof row marked: "Caught with proof".
- Exactly one proof row per risky plan (content migration; emulated as the last red row). With the display shuffle, row 0 stays fixed.
- A blind Escalate has no proof.
- A rolled-back risky plan needs no proof and grades "Caught it late" (P).

STARS
- 1st star: won.
- 2nd star: no miss. A rolled-back plan is not a miss.
- 3rd star: at most 1 false alarm AND every Block or Escalate catch had proof.
- Rejected, measured:
  - Roll Back costs the 3rd star: the triage payoff disappears (triage bot 26-85%).
  - One shared slip allowed: careful 73-96%, guess-flag 3-9%.
  - Escalate exempt from proof: careful 80-100%, guess-flag up to 3.5%.

ENGINE WORK (when built)
- Coffee energy branch.
- Encounter fields: exhaust, stopGuarantee, wrapUp.
- CARDS costs and texts.
- A stakesOf(step) helper plus the chip in IntentCard.
- StepRuntime.clue and BattleState.grading as in grading-impact.md.
- Story encounter JSON: deck, unlocks, order. DAILY_DECK, plus a per-pathway extra card for BA.
designs.sim_results:
Run: the real engine through the harness copy (design-scarcity/sim). 1000 story seeds and 1800 daily runs per pathway (600 dailies × 3 deck shuffles). 3-star rule: proof (one proof row). Cloud & Network, Full-Stack and Business Analyst stories have the same structure, so their story numbers are identical.

BANDS: 28 of 30 checks pass. Both failures are guess-flag in dailies (Help Desk 1.8%, Business Analyst 1.1%, against a limit of ≤1%).

CAREFUL BOT 3 STARS (band 40-70%)
| Pathway | Story | Daily |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Help Desk | 54.2 | 53.2 |
| Cybersecurity | 59.2 | 48.3 |
| Cloud & Network | 49.2 | 62.6 |
| Full-Stack | 49.2 | 67.2 |
| Business Analyst | 49.2 | 64.8 |

- Careful wins 100% everywhere. Daily pass is 98.5-99.7%.

TRIAGE TURNS (careful runs with at least one triage turn; band ≥60%)
- Story: HD 69.0, CY 75.2, CN/FS/BA 62.1.
- Daily: 83.8-94.1.
- Per turn, story (careful): HD turn 3 11.6%, turn 4 28.1%, turn 5 33.3%. CY turn 3 36.5%, turn 5 55.5%. CN/FS/BA turn 4 50.8%, turn 5 11.3%.
- Turns 1-2 never force a triage.
- Turn 1: 0% dead; careful plays a card there in 98-100% of runs (the policy).

SKILL GAP: triage bot (badge-guided) vs the same bot in random order (no badge)
| Pathway | Story | Daily |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Help Desk | 96.2 vs 62.6 | 84.6 vs 57.2 |
| Cybersecurity | 100 vs 61.9 | 79.0 vs 47.7 |
| CN/FS/BA | 95.3 vs 71.0 | 76-85 vs 60-63 |

- The badge is worth +24 to +38 points in the story and +16 to +31 in dailies.

DEGENERATE BOTS
- approve-all: 0% win or pass everywhere.
- block-all: story 0%; daily pass 0-1.3%.
- escalate-unknown (the buck-passer): 0% everywhere. Baseline daily pass was 5.8-17%.
- random: story win 27.7-32.4%, daily pass 9.7-15.2%, 0 stars.
- gut-flag: 0% 3 stars.
- guess-flag 3 stars: story 0.1-0.2%; daily HD 1.8, BA 1.1, CN 0.8, FS 0.7, CY 0.3. Padding every plan to 4 rows barely moves it (HD 1.5 → 1.3). It is the arithmetic of random picks across 2-3 catches.

LUCK
- Card-luck misses (red flag up, no Block or usable Escalate card in hand at all): 0.0% in all 10 cells. Baseline dailies: 2.3-4.3%.
- No playable stop, energy included (careful spent its energy on Inspects): story 0-3.7%, daily 0.9-6.9%.

UNUSED ENERGY PER RUN (not improved)
- Story 2.5-3.2 (baseline 2.0-4.0). Daily 3.9-7.2 (baseline 3.1-7.1). Inspect cards are the scarce thing, not energy.

HUMAN-LIKE CLUE READERS (3 stars)
- Finds the proof row 80% of the time:
  - Careful (in order): story 20.5-25.5, daily 23-30.1.
  - Triage (badge): story 40.1-52.9, daily 37-42.6.
  - Same rules without scarcity: careful 33-42 story, 24.5-39.6 daily; triage 35-42 story, 27-41 daily.
- Mixed ESL (proof 50%, wrong row 20%, no mark 30%): careful 3.5-6.7, triage 6.3-14.4. Same rules without scarcity: 4-8.

CARDS (careful, % of runs played)
- Inspect 100; Block ~100.
- Policy: 100 story, 54-84 daily.
- Escalate: 38-49 story, 46-66 daily.
- Roll Back: careful 0-2 story, 17-34 daily. The triage bot uses it up to 0.98 times per run in CY.
- Coffee: 0-4.8.

ABLATION (remove one copy, change in careful 3 stars)
- One Inspect: -32 to -59 story, -13 to -21 daily.
- Coffee: +0 to +13 (only as deck filler).
- No Coffee at all breaks the bands: CN/FS/BA story triage turns 56%; FS and BA daily 72 and 78.5.

COMPARISON (same harness, same run sizes)
- Shipped baseline: careful story 92.8-100 and daily 75.5-94.1 (any red row counts as proof); triage turns story 6.4-18.1, daily 45-70; guess-flag 6-17.
- Phase 2 rules without scarcity: careful story 78.8-99.4, daily 53.6-88.7; triage turns story 6.4-18.1.

SWEEPS BEHIND THE CHOICES: sc-1, sc-2, sc-d1, sc-hd, sc-hd2, sc-coffee, sc-coffee2, sc-coffee3, sc-energy, sc-glance, sc-slips, sc-escproof, sc-pol3, sc-ba, sc-final, sc-guess.

HARNESS BUGS FOUND in the shared phase2/sim (fixed in my copy only)
- The wrap-up beat never fired: knownBad() calls validTargets on a finished battle, which returns []. With the fix, p2-candidate careful 3 stars go from 36.5-45 to 50-60.5 in dailies and from 70.3 to 79 in the Help Desk story. variants/p2c-nowrap.json reproduces the original numbers exactly.
- The stop guarantee counted a spent Escalate as a stop card (0.2-1% card-luck misses).

designs.player_experience:
Example: Cloud & Network story, turn 4 (the busiest turn), on a 390 px phone.

SCREEN A: the board (about 35 words)
- Nimbus announces 3 plans. Each card has: order number, intent (about 5 words), the stakes chip (icon + 1-2 words), and a status icon.
  - 1 "Call Cairnholt's support line" [eye] Look only · Not checked
  - 2 "Stop the 6 test servers" [undo] Can undo · Checked by policy
  - 3 "Delete the old Pinecrest archive" [lock] One-way · Not checked
- Hand: Inspect, Block, Block, Roll Back, Escalate. Energy 3.
- The coach's one-line hint appears only in the first story shift: "1 Inspect. Check the One-way plan first." (8 words)
- ONE decision: which plan gets your only check.

SCREEN B: evidence sheet for plan 3 (about 40 words)
- 4 rows of label + fact, about 8 words each. Row 0 ("Change ticket") is always first. Nimbus's quip is at the top in its voice, e.g. "Old means useless. That's just science."
- The player taps the line that looks wrong (Phase 1a mark). This is now the clue.
- Buttons: Block / Let it run.
- ONE decision: block it, and which line proves it.

SCREEN C: result toast (3-5 words)
- "Caught with proof" (or "Right call, wrong clue"), plus the stage vignette.
- Energy 1 left. Plan 1 is Look only and plan 2 was checked by the policy.

SCREEN D: back to the board, now 2 plans
- ONE decision: tap "Approve" (end turn).
- If the player had instead let a Can-undo plan run and it went wrong, the risk meter rises and the stage shows it. Next turn, Roll Back (cost 1) is the fix: "Caught it late".

SCREEN E: plans run
- Each plan gets a 1-line result on the stage (about 10 words total).

OTHER BEATS
- Turn 1 of the story: 1 scary-looking-but-safe plan ("Fail over Harlow & Cole's app", [undo] Can undo). The Policy card costs 2.
  - Tap Policy (1 decision). The plan flips to "Checked by policy". Open it if you like, then Approve. About 25 words.
- Last turn: if a Can-undo plan went bad, the wrap-up beat shows 1 prompt, "One more thing: undo it?", with Roll Back already in hand.
designs.cognitive_load:
One new thing to read, and nothing new to count.
- The only addition to the board is a 1-2 word stakes chip with an icon on each plan card.
- The chip is the same 3 words everywhere: One-way, Can undo, Look only.
- It maps directly onto the question the coach already asks: "Can we undo it?"

The judge's extra counters were cut:
- Escalate becomes a normal Exhaust card ("Once per shift"). No budget number to track.
- Coffee has one plain effect: "+1 energy".
- There is no glance sentence. Measured: it gives no information, and it would add a line to every card on a phone.

Every screen still holds one decision:
- Board: which plan gets my check.
- Sheet: Block or Let it run, plus mark the line (both existing).
- Toast: none.
- End turn: Approve.

Other load controls:
- Scarcity arrives gradually. Turns 1-2 never force a triage, so the first story minutes stay calm. Pressure starts on turns 3-5.
- Turn 1 teaches the badge and the policy with a single tap.
- The story deck still has 5 card types, the same as today.
- No new rules text is longer than 8 words.
- The coach teaches the badge with one hint line in the first story shift only.
- Humor stays in the agent's quip, which is shown on the card when there is room and in the sheet otherwise.

Accessibility: the chip needs its own aria text, e.g. "Plan 3: Delete the old Pinecrest archive. One-way. Not checked." It also needs an icon plus a word (not colour alone) and a contrast check in both themes.
designs.risks:
1. Real players will rarely earn 3 stars.
- The 40-70% band assumes a bot that always marks the proof row.
- A player who finds the proof row 80% of the time gets 3 stars in 20-30% of careful runs, and 37-53% if they read the badge.
- The mixed-ESL model gets 3.5-14%.
- Tune with playtest clue accuracy, not by loosening the rule. Loosening measured badly: one slip allowed puts guess-flag at 3-9%; exempting Escalate puts careful at 80-100%.
- Consider showing proof progress (e.g. "Proof 3/4") so a missed 3rd star still feels like progress.

2. Coffee "+1 energy" is almost a dead card.
- It is played in 0-4.8% of careful runs, because Inspect cards are scarce, not energy.
- It stays only as deck filler: removing it breaks the bands (CN/FS/BA story triage turns 56%; FS and BA daily careful 72 and 78.5).
- Draw 1 is a useful alternative: careful up 5-22 points, but 2 cells land just over 70.
- Draw 2 swings CN/FS/BA stories to 100%.

3. "Let it run, then Roll Back" is the dominant good-play line, and it can teach a wrong lesson.
- Rolled-back plans keep the 3rd star, and the triage bot leans on Roll Back (up to 0.98 per run in CY).
- Some plans marked reversible are not harmless once run (an MFA reset for an impostor can't be un-logged-in).
- The content needs a reversibility audit: mark "harm can't be undone" plans as One-way even if the setting can be undone. Otherwise the badge will be wrong.
- Keep "Caught it late" graded P, with a coach line.

4. "Look only" plans are always safe (35 of 35).
- For those plans, the badge reveals the answer.
- Acceptable (reading is low-stakes), but it can teach "read-only means safe". Future bank content should add risky lookups (e.g. looking up a record for an unverified asker).

5. The tuning is invisible and differs per pathway.
- Help Desk: 3 Inspects, Callback at cost 1, reordered story.
- Business Analyst dailies: +1 Block.
- These are principled (they follow policy coverage) but must be pinned per pathway in balance.test.
- Careful story results depend on reading the plans top-down: the Help Desk turn-4 order moves careful from 38 to 54. A player picking plans at random lands at 62-71%.

6. Expert play nearly always earns 3 stars (triage bot 95-100% in the story). The stars stop telling experts apart.

7. guess-flag is 1.1-1.8% in Help Desk and Business Analyst dailies (limit ≤1%). Random picks can never reach exactly 0. Content with 4 rows per plan helps only slightly (1.5 → 1.3).

8. Unused energy is not reduced (story 2.5-3.2 per run). The energy orb matters less than the Inspect count.

9. Numbers are emulated, not engine-run.
- Emulated in the harness: the stop guarantee, wrap-up beat, Coffee energy, clue and proof, the badge-guided bot, and Escalate Exhaust (done in the harness through the global CARDS, so drills were not simulated).
- When built:
  - Put the Escalate Exhaust on the encounter, so practice and drills keep today's Escalate.
  - Remove the emulation and rerun: the numbers must not move.
  - Port the fixed wrap-up and stop-guarantee code back to phase2/sim. The p2-candidate numbers that other designers used were measured with the wrap-up beat broken.

10. Golden and saves.
- Changes to the Help Desk golden: the "story" section, "built", "cards" (Roll Back cost, Coffee and Escalate text), all 48 story traces and all 8 daily traces.
- The 24 practice traces and 32 drill traces must stay byte-identical. Audit that.
- Recapture in 4 audited steps, each logged in the golden.test.ts header:
  - (a) engine mechanics only;
  - (b) encounter deck, unlocks and order, plus DAILY_DECK;
  - (c) proof grading, per grading-impact.md, with the "proof" and "guess" play styles added first;
  - (d) content (proof row, undoNotes).
- Every pathway's deck changes, so canResume rejects in-progress story and daily saves, and players restart that shift. History, skills, bankVersion and daily/drill specs survive. Practice and drill saves resume. Say so in the release note.

designs.name: Name the Clue (depth over breadth)
designs.pitch:
Every Inspect card stays. Every hand is guaranteed at least one Inspect and one Block. Finding the right line becomes the skill that earns the 3rd star. Pressure comes from the clock and the stakes, not from cutting cards:
- The story has a rush turn (3 plans, 3 energy).
- Dailies announce 2 plans a turn from turn 1.
- Each plan card carries a 3-way badge: One-way, Can undo, or Read-only.
- Roll Back costs 1 and is in the starter deck. Letting a Can-undo plan run and undoing it is a real move, but it keeps only 2 stars.

Stars: ★ shift done, ★★ no damage left, ★★★ you stopped every bad plan before it ran and marked its clue.

Measured on the real engine (private copy, engine-native, no emulation), all 5 pathways, story and daily:
- The design meets every band.
- Every seed stays winnable with 3 stars.
- A skilled player who knows the answers (the oracle bot) gets 3 stars in 100% of runs.

Caveat: dailies meet the bands, but their pressure comes mostly from hands with a single Inspect, not from the clock.
designs.rules:
All rule changes are engine-native in the private copy. Each is opt-in through a new optional `Encounter.rules`, so the engine alone changes nothing: 818 of 818 lib/game tests pass without content changes.

CARDS (energy 3 per turn and hand 5 stay the same):
- Inspect: 4 copies, cost 1, unchanged.
- Block: 3 copies, cost 1, unchanged.
- Roll Back: cost 2 → 1. It moves into the story starter deck (it used to unlock on turn 4). The daily deck is unchanged.
- Escalate: cost 2. New shift budget of 1 (`rules.escalateBudget`). Refusal line: "{Coach} is busy. No more escalations this shift." Unlocks on story turn 3, as today.
- Policy (all 5): cost 1 → 2. Story unlock moves from turn 2 to turn 1, so turn 1 has a real choice: look at both plans, or buy the policy and look at one. It still exhausts. The daily rule is unchanged (added when it covers a plan).
- Coffee: "Draw 2" becomes "+1 energy this turn" (`CardDef.energy`, cost 0, exhaust). In the story it unlocks on turn 4 (was turn 5), the rush turn.

HAND FLOOR (`rules.stopGuarantee` + `inspectFloor: 1`):
- After the draw and before unlocks, every hand holds at least 1 Block and 1 Inspect.
- A missing card is swapped in from the draw pile, then the discard pile, replacing the last non-floor card. No RNG; the deck itself is unchanged.
- It guarantees a Block, not "any stop", because an Escalate may be over budget.

PLANS PER TURN:
- Story: [1,2,2,3] becomes [2,2,2,3,1]. Turn 4 is the rush turn (3 plans). maxTurns stays 6.
- Each story gets its own order. Each ticket keeps its internal order, and plan 1 is safe:
  - Help Desk: ruiz-vpn-fix, okafor-disable, romero-lookup, ruiz-vpn-close!, okafor-mail-forward, romero-mfa-reset!, ortiz-laptop, okafor-summary!, ortiz-unlock, ortiz-access!
  - Cybersecurity: cy-lam-report-real, cy-dsp04-isolate, cy-whitcomb-signins, cy-duarte-report-close!, cy-sandoval-disable, cy-whitcomb-disable!, cy-sandoval-wipe!, cy-c2-deny, cy-sandoval-hr-list, cy-ransom-close!
  - Cloud & Network: cn-dispatch-errors, cn-dispatch-close!, cn-hc-failover, cn-stonebridge-tunnel!, cn-stonebridge-call, cn-pd-orphan-disks, cn-dispatch-log-vendor, cn-test-servers-stop, cn-dispatch-scale-zero!, cn-pd-archive-delete!
  - Full-Stack: fs-track-errors, fs-track-close!, fs-lark-package!, fs-pd-key-rotate, fs-track-test-data, fs-pd-cleanup!, fs-hc-flag-off, fs-hc-date-fix, fs-hc-late-release!, fs-lark-docs
  - Business Analyst: ba-ontime-compare, ba-ontime-close!, ba-lark-share!, ba-hc-unpublish, ba-wayfell-sample, ba-pd-export-delete, ba-lark-owner, ba-hc-deck-share, ba-hc-ontime-rule!, ba-pd-merge!
  - No turn has 2 risky plans. A pair makes 3 stars impossible at 3 energy, because a proof catch costs 2.
- Dailies: DAILY_ACTIONS_PER_TURN [1,2] becomes [2,2]. The generator's order rules are unchanged (never 2 risky plans on one turn; plan 1 is a plain safe plan) and re-order for the new shape. maxTurns stays 7.

DECK: story starter is 4 Inspect, 3 Block, 1 Roll Back. Unlocks: turn 1 policy, turn 3 Escalate, turn 4 Coffee.

GLANCE LINE: dropped. Row 0 is never red in any of the 125 risky plans, so a free glance carries no information.

STAKES BADGE: a 3-way badge derived from existing fields, with no content change:
- Read-only = category "lookup"
- Can undo = reversible
- One-way = everything else

A 2-way badge does not help triage, because every lookup is labelled one-way and safe (measured below). One-time rush-turn tip: "Not enough energy for all 3? Look at One-way first."

CLUE GRADING (rule A, mastery.gradePlan):
- On Block or Escalate the engine stores `StepRuntime.clue` (content index; a bad index counts as no mark and never blocks the play) and freezes `StepRuntime.proof` = plan was seen + clue is its proof row.
- Proof row = the one `Evidence.proof` row per risky plan. The migration stand-in is the last red row.
- Grades:
  - Proof: R "Caught with proof".
  - No mark: R "Caught" (skill levels stay as today).
  - Wrong mark: P "Right call, wrong clue".
  - Stopping a plan never looked at keeps today's P ("Lucky guess" / coach).
  - A rolled-back plan stays P "Caught it late".
- Practice stores the mark but never grades it.

STARS (scoreBattle when `BattleState.grading === "proof"`):
- ★ Won.
- ★★ No damage left: no standing miss. A Roll Back clears a Can-undo miss.
- ★★★ Every risky plan was stopped before it ran (Block or Escalate) with its proof line marked, and at most 1 false alarm. A Roll Back rescue costs this star (`rules.rollbackCosts3rd`).

This replaces the blind-block check and also closes today's "escalate blind for 3 stars" loophole. The "lucky" headline now fires on unproven stops.

SAVES:
- `grading` is set only on new battles, and `version` stays 1.
- Old story saves restart. canResume already rejects them: 0 of 1500 old mid-shift saves resume, because the deck changed. Say so in the release note.
- Dailies need a new `ShiftSpec` marker. Unmarked specs must rebuild as Phase 1 ([1,2], no rules). canResume accepts 60 of 60 old daily saves, but 18-39 of 60 old orders per pathway break the new "no 2 risky on one turn" rule under [2,2].

CONTENT PREREQUISITES (same release):
- Exactly one proof row per risky plan (123 plans).
- Unflag the 43 rule rows.
- Seeded display shuffle.
- Verdict words move to a review-only `Evidence.check`, with a lint.
- Rewrite the story coach tips for the new order.

Each screen asks one thing:
- the board: which plan to look at;
- the sheet: which line is wrong;
- the marked sheet: Block or Looks OK;
- the board again: look again, or Approve the rest.

The only new visible elements are a 1-2 word stakes badge on each plan card, a clue line that already exists from Phase 1a, and 3 star lines of 7 words or fewer.

Things that were cut or kept invisible:
- The glance line is cut; it carried no information.
- The hand floor is invisible. The player just never meets a hand with no way to look or stop.
- Coffee becomes the simplest possible effect, "+1 energy", instead of drawing cards to manage.
- Escalate says no in one line when its budget is used.

The 3rd star has one plain rule: stop every bad plan before it runs, and mark why.

For ESL learners and the 13+ audience:
- Grading never punishes silence. A player who never marks keeps "Caught" and today's skill levels.
- A wrong mark is "Right call", partly right, never a loss.
- Practice records marks but never grades them.

Every new sentence is 10 words or fewer, in present tense, with no idioms. The humor stays in the agent's quips. The pressure is a count the player can see ("3 plans, 3 energy"), not hidden odds.

1. 3 stars become an expert badge. A player who finds the clue 80% of the time gets 3 stars in only 20-36% of runs; the mixed ESL player gets 3-7%. Mitigation: make "No damage left" (2 stars) the celebrated goal, and tune with playtest clue accuracy.

designs.name: Rush Hour (tempo): waves, stakes badges, check now or fix it on the calm turn
designs.pitch:
Ollie's plans now come in waves: 2 plans, then a rush of 3, then 1 calm plan, then a rush of 3, then 1. You can't check a whole rush and still stop what you find, so the choice each rush is WHEN to check and HOW DEEP.

Every plan card carries a free "One-way" or "Can undo" badge, and a one-line "Next up" strip shows the next wave. One-way plans must be checked and stopped before they run. Can-undo plans can wait: you can check them after they run and undo them, but only until the end of the next turn, and only if you still have your one Roll Back. One unused energy carries over, so a quiet turn buys you room for the rush or for fixing a mistake.

The skill it teaches is the coach's third question, "Can we undo it?", used as a way to prioritize, not just as a fact. It is measured with the real engine in all 5 pathways:
- **Stories:** careful in-order play gets 3 stars in 49-58% of runs. A player who handles one-way plans first gets 70-79%.
- **Dailies:** careful gets 3 stars in 45-64% of runs.
- **Guards:** approve-all and block-all fail, and no run loses to card luck it couldn't fix.
designs.rules:
These are the exact changes, all measured. Engine knobs are optional encounter fields; when a field is absent the game behaves as today. With them absent, all 818 game tests and the Help Desk golden pass byte-identical, and typecheck is clean.

1. WAVES AND PLANS PER TURN.
- **Story:** actionsPerTurn [2,3,1,3,1] (10 plans), maxTurns 6 (one spare turn). Was [1,2,2,3].
- **Daily:** the same waves (DAILY_ACTIONS_PER_TURN), maxTurns 7. Was [1,2].
- **"Next up" strip (UI only):** the next wave's plan titles and badges. No evidence.

2. STAKES BADGE.
- Every plan card shows "One-way" or "Can undo", read from the existing `reversible` field. No new content needed.
- The badge tells priority, not the verdict. Risky share is about the same under each badge (Help Desk one-way 39% risky vs can-undo 45%).
- Lookups are "One-way". Do not add a "Read only" badge: lookups are 0% risky, so that badge would leak the answer.

3. GLANCE LINE: none.
- The free glance is the card itself: title, badge and quip (the quip needs the content audit's rewrite).
- The balance harness found evidence row 0 is never red in any of the 125 risky plans, so showing it adds words and zero triage information. Revisit only if content authors a telling row 0.

4. ENERGY.
- 3 per turn, and up to 1 unused point carries over (carryEnergy: 1). The energy pip shows "+1 saved".
- Measured: carry 0 gives careful 0% 3 stars in the Help Desk and Cybersecurity stories. Carry 2 gives 86-94% (too easy).

5. LATE CHECK ("Check it later").
- Inspect (cost 1) may also target a done can-undo plan that is still inside its undo window (lateCheck: true).
- A free late check measured about the same as a 1-energy one, so it stays at cost 1 (simpler).

6. UNDO WINDOW.
- Roll Back works only until the end of the turn after the plan ran (undoWindow: 1). Cost stays 2.
- Measured: cost 1 is too easy (86-94%). Cost 3 kills recovery (careful 0-6% in 4 stories).
- The window halves watch-undo's daily passes (Business Analyst 25% to 15.5%, Full-Stack 15.5% to 7.5%).

7. FAIRNESS.
- Every new hand holds a Block or Escalate (oneWayStop: "always"). If it has none, one is swapped in from the draw or discard pile for a non-Inspect card, without RNG. Unfixable card-luck misses drop to 0 in all 10 story and daily cells.
- A "Roll Back guarantee" was measured and rejected. With it, watch-undo passes 28-62% of dailies and careful drops to 11% in the Help Desk story. Keeping undo scarce is what makes checking before a plan runs worth it.

8. CARDS AND STORY DECK.
- **Starter deck:** 4 Inspect, 3 Block, 1 Roll Back. Roll Back moves from the turn-4 unlock into the starter deck.
- **Unlocks:** turn 2 policy (cost 1, unchanged), turn 3 Escalate (cost 2), turn 5 Coffee (draw 2, unchanged).
- **Not adopted from the judge's draft:** no Coffee-as-energy, no Escalate budget, no cost-2 policy. None is needed to reach the bands. The balance harness showed a cost-2 policy on turn 2 drops careful to 0% 3 stars in every story.
- **Story risk limit 8** (was 10). watch-undo's story win rate drops from 75% to 0%, and careful still wins 99.6-100%.

9. STORY ORDER, per pathway. The layout grammar: the opener is unchanged; turn 1 holds 2 safe plans; each rush wave holds a one-way plan, 1-2 risky plans and at most 1 one-way risky plan, which comes last; each ticket's plans stay in order. Found by an exhaustive search of every legal order (648-2,304 per pathway), then 400-seed re-measures, then 1000-seed confirmation:
- **Help Desk:** romero-lookup, ortiz-laptop | ruiz-vpn-fix, ruiz-vpn-close, okafor-disable | okafor-mail-forward | romero-mfa-reset, ortiz-unlock, okafor-summary | ortiz-access
- **Cybersecurity:** cy-whitcomb-signins, cy-sandoval-disable | cy-whitcomb-disable, cy-dsp04-isolate, cy-sandoval-wipe | cy-c2-deny | cy-sandoval-hr-list, cy-ransom-close, cy-lam-report-real | cy-duarte-report-close
- **Cloud & Network:** cn-dispatch-errors, cn-hc-failover | cn-dispatch-close, cn-pd-orphan-disks, cn-dispatch-log-vendor | cn-stonebridge-tunnel | cn-test-servers-stop, cn-dispatch-scale-zero, cn-pd-archive-delete | cn-stonebridge-call
- **Full-Stack:** fs-track-errors, fs-hc-flag-off | fs-track-close, fs-pd-key-rotate, fs-track-test-data | fs-lark-package | fs-hc-date-fix, fs-hc-late-release, fs-pd-cleanup | fs-lark-docs
- **Business Analyst:** ba-ontime-compare, ba-hc-unpublish | ba-hc-deck-share, ba-pd-export-delete, ba-lark-share | ba-hc-ontime-rule | ba-ontime-close, ba-pd-merge, ba-wayfell-sample | ba-lark-owner

10. DAILY GENERATOR (shiftGen DAILY_ORDER, real code in the private copy). Order rules:
- Each wave of 3 or more plans holds a one-way plan.
- At most 1 one-way risky plan per wave, and it comes last.
- Never 2 risky plans in a row.
- Risky plans per wave: at most 1 in Help Desk and Cybersecurity, at most 2 in the other three. This needs a new per-pathway shift.json field.
- 100% of generated dailies satisfy these rules.

Daily deck: +1 Inspect for every pathway, and +1 more when the policy covers under 20% of the bank. Only Help Desk qualifies: its policy covers 10% of its plans and 14% of its risky plans, versus 29-50% elsewhere.

11. CLUE GRADING. Block, Escalate and Roll Back on a risky plan all carry the marked line.
- It counts as proof only when it is the plan's single proof row (the content audit's "one proof row per risky plan"; the harness uses the last red row) on a plan the player saw, before it ran or through a late check.
- Store the mark as the row label (content audit).
- Mastery uses the grading agent's rule A: no mark = R "Caught"; wrong mark = P "Right call, wrong clue". A Roll Back of a risky plan stays P "Caught it late".

12. STARS.
- 1 star = won.
- 2nd star = nothing got through. A plan that was rolled back is not a miss, as today.
- 3rd star = at most 1 false alarm, and every stop on a risky plan (Block, Escalate or Roll Back, the "late catch") had the proof row marked.

13. DAILY PASS (recommended, independent of tempo): won, at most 1 W, and at least half the risky plans graded R.

designs.cognitive_load:
**One decision per screen:**
- Board: "which plan do I check?"
- Sheet: "stop it or let it run?" (marking a line is optional and ungraded for mastery under rule A).
- End of turn: Approve.
- Calm turn: "fix it or not?"

**New concepts: three, each shown only where it's used.**
- **The badge (2 words on the card):** it replaces reading the evidence to decide priority. It uses an existing content field and the coach's existing third question, "Can we undo it?".
- **"+1 saved" on the energy pip:** no rule text needed. The player just sees they have 4.
- **"Undo until next turn" on done-plan chips:** it appears only after a can-undo plan ran.

**No new cards.** Inspect gains done plans as targets, and Roll Back already exists. Target lists stay separate on screen: the board for plans that haven't run, a done strip for plans that have. A naive player might otherwise spend an Inspect on a done plan.

**Removed from the judge's draft on purpose, because they measured as no gain for extra words:**
- the glance evidence line (row 0 is never red)
- Coffee-as-energy
- the Escalate budget
- the blame fog
- "spotted it, no card"

**Pacing and teaching:**
- The rhythm 2 / 3 / 1 / 3 / 1 gives a breather after every rush. The calm turn is where fixing happens, so the player is never asked to triage and repair on the same screen.
- The first rush of the first shift gets one 8-word coach line. After that, no tips.
- Practice is unchanged, so the golden practice traces stay identical. Adding one practice line about the badge is a later, optional step.

**ESL:** the badge words are short and concrete ("One-way", "Can undo"). Chips use present-tense fragments, and there are no numbers in rules text except energy costs already on the cards.

**Accessibility:**
- Badge and chip state are carried by text plus an icon, never color alone.
- The Next up strip is a single line.
- A saved-energy change is announced once via the existing toast region.

plan.chosen_design:
A Depth ("Name the Clue") backbone with four measured director changes, plus parts of Scarcity and Tempo.

SCORES (1-5; for load and build risk, 5 = lowest load and lowest risk):

| Design | Fun | Learning | Load | Balance evidence | Build risk | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Scarcity | 3 | 3.5 | 4.5 | 3 | 3 | 17 |
| Depth | 3.5 | 4.5 | 4 | 5 | 4 | 21 |
| Tempo | 4.5 | 3.5 | 2 | 3.5 | 2 | 15.5 |

Why Depth:
- It is engine-native. Harness and engine agree on 45,500 of 45,500 runs, and the applied content reproduces the numbers exactly.
- It meets every band in all 10 pathway and mode cells.
- Every seed can reach 3 stars.
- It keeps the lesson: stop it before it runs, and say why.

Why not Scarcity:
- It is emulated, not engine-native, and 2 of its 30 band checks fail.
- Roll Back becomes the dominant play, and Coffee is a dead card.

Why not Tempo:
- It has the best rhythm, but it adds 3 new ideas: saved energy, an undo timer and checks on plans that already ran.
- It also needs a Done strip, per-pathway generator rules and fragile searched layouts. That is too much for ESL phone players.

The four director changes, each measured in phase2/director/sim:
1. Escalate becomes "Once per shift" (it exhausts) instead of a budget counter. This is Scarcity's idea: no counter and no refusal message. Story numbers are identical; dailies move by 1.5 points or less.
2. Story turn 1 is 2 safe plans in all 5 pathways, at least one of them scary-safe.
   - I found that Depth's cost-2 policy on turn 1 is a trap in Cloud & Network, Full-Stack and Business Analyst: buying it at once gives 0% three stars.
   - I re-searched those 3 layouts (83-101 legal orders each, 16-18 pass). Now buying the policy early is a rewarded investment: story 80-100% vs careful 56-67%. Buying it eagerly in dailies is slightly worse, so judgment matters.
   - Rejected: policy on turn 2 (Cloud & Network and Business Analyst careful 92%, too easy) and Callback at cost 1 (Help Desk 80.3%).
3. The badge words are "One-way / Can undo / Look only". The third tier stays, because it measured +7 to +39 points of triage value.
4. The clue has three grades:
   - proof row: R "Caught with proof";
   - another real red row: R "Caught";
   - a plain row: P "Right stop, wrong line";
   - no mark: R "Caught" (rule A).

   Only the proof row earns the 3rd star, so a player who marks a real warning sign is never told they were wrong.

Other sources:
- From Tempo: no badge word that means "safe", and the one-time rush-turn tip.
- From the grading plan: rule A, and a battle-level grading flag instead of a version bump.
- From the content audit: unflag the rule rows, one proof row per risky plan, the display shuffle now, and verdict text moved to review-only `check` later.

Rejected, with the measurement behind each:

| Idea | Why not |
|---|---|
| Free glance line | Row 0 is never red in 125 of 125 risky plans |
| Wrap-up Roll Back beat | No effect on careful play |
| "Spotted it, no card" | Raises random daily pass from 12% to 21.5% |
| Escalate budget counter | Replaced by Exhaust |
| 2 Inspects | Roll Back becomes the dominant play |
| Energy carry and undo window | Too much to take in |

Final measured results (2000 story seeds; 400 dailies x 3 shuffles; proof rule; values for HD/CY/CN/FS/BA):

| Measure | Story | Daily |
|---|---|---|
| Careful 3 stars | 58.6/67.4/67.2/60.7/56.1 | 50.1/45.3/51.9/45.3/43.1 |
| Careful runs with a triage turn | 68.6-83.7 | 84.7-89.8 |
| Triage bot (reads the badge) 3 stars | 81.9-92.9 | (info only) |
| Policy-investor bot 3 stars | 80.3-100 | (info only) |
| Guess-flag 3 stars | 0.2-0.4 | 0.3-0.6 |
| Oracle 3 stars | 100 | (info only) |
| Careful win / daily pass | 100 | 99.2-99.7 |
| approve-all, block-all, escalate-unknown win or pass | 0 | 0.1 or less |

Rerunning on content where my script sets the proof rows gives identical numbers for every bot except guess-flag, which moves by 0.4 points or less.

problems: P1: The 3-star bands are tuned on a bot that always marks the right line, not on the players we have. The 'careful' bot marks the proof row every time. With the plan's final rules, careful gets 3 stars in 43-67% of shifts. The bot that finds the right line 80% of the time (human80) gets 19-38%. The ESL-style mixed bot (esl-mix: right 50%, wrong 20%, no mark 30%) gets 3.5-6.5%. The proof star alone, on today's layouts, already puts human80 at 33-44% and esl-mix at 5-9% (critic/sim/results/c-proofOnly.json). So the new card economy and layouts mostly lower the perfect-reader number. For real players, reading accuracy decides the star, and the ~20 points the economy takes off careful come on top of that. The owner summary line 'Careful play earns 3 stars in 43-67%' will mislead the owner.

P2: Wrong habit: the plan penalizes 'can't check it, so escalate'. The UI says 'Not sure? Escalate' (EvidencePanel.tsx:374). Under the proof rule, escalating a plan you never inspected costs the 3rd star. Much of careful's star loss comes from this correct real-world call. When one unseen Escalate is allowed to count (Escalate already exhausts, so it is capped at once per shift), careful rises from 58.5/66.9/66.4 to 83/88.2/92 in the HD/CY/CN story and from 43-52 to 71-79 in dailies. Degenerate bots stay at 0 (escalate-unknown 0% win and 0% pass) and guess-flag stays at or below 2.3% (critic/sim/results/c-blindEscOk.json). Where the gap between careful and this variant is large (HD, CY, CN; FS and BA barely move), the careful bot's missing 3-stars come mostly from asking for help at the right time.

P3: The Look only badge teaches that read-only plans are safe, which is the opposite of the lesson. All 23 lookup plans (7 story, 16 bank) are safe. The measured '+7 to +39 triage value' is almost all this leak. With the Look only tier turned off (critic/sim/results/c-noRO.json), triage minus careful is: story HD +8.4, CY 0, CN 0, FS 0, BA +10.1; dailies HD +8.7, CY -2.9, CN -5.8, FS -3.8, BA -3.0. The 'triage >= careful + 10' band passes only because of the leak. The bot's winning move is to approve read-only plans without looking, which is exactly how agents leak data. The plan defers risky Look only plans to 2c, after the badge ships.

P4: The One-way / Can undo badge and its coach tip fight the scoring. Content shows One-way plans are not riskier: story 5/12 risky (42%) vs Can undo 15/31 (48%); bank 26/73 (36%) vs 77/158 (49%). The tip's logic is 'you can fix Can undo later', but rollbackCosts3rd makes fixing it later cost the 3rd star. Turning rollbackCosts3rd off (critic/sim/results/c-noRB3-noRO.json, no Look only leak) gives badge triage a real edge in dailies: +17.3 HD, +14.5 CY, +4.9 CN, +17 FS, +17 BA. With it on, that edge is -6 to +9. So as specified, the chip's real lesson (triage by impact) is not rewarded.

P5: In 2a the proof row is a script's pick among real warning signs. After scripts/proof-rows.py, 15 of 20 story risky plans and 71 of 103 bank risky plans still have 2-3 red rows. A player who marks the other genuine red row is told 'Caught! The key clue: X' and silently loses the 3rd star. No writer has checked the picks until 2b/2c. Counting any real red row as proof raises human80 by 6-14 points (story 39.8-48.2) but lets guess-flag reach 1.0-4.1% (critic/sim/results/c-flagcounts.json).

P6: Save claim is false. The plan says in-progress story battles restart because the deck changed. I ran the live engine: a pre-2a story save at turn 5 or later passes canResume against the new layout in all 5 pathways. The old turn-5 deck (4 Inspect, 3 Block, policy, Escalate, Roll Back, Coffee) equals the new deckAtTurn(5) (critic/savecheck.mjs). That save would resume with its old queue but the new actionsPerTurn, new encounter rules and new card costs, and no grading flag. Separately, pre-2a dailies do not resume 'under today's rules': CARDS is global, so Coffee becomes +1 energy, Roll Back costs 1 and the policy costs 2 in the middle of a resumed battle.

P7: Wrong-mark grading discourages trying. Rule A gives no mark = R but a wrong plain line = P ('Right stop, wrong line'). For mastery, never marking beats marking when unsure. That discourages the retrieval attempt the stage exists to build. The reason string is saved permanently, so this must be decided before shipping.

P8: Turn 1 of the first-ever story shift now adds 3 new things at once: a second plan, a new badge vocabulary on every card, and a cost-2 Policy card whose payoff comes later and is never explained. That choice alone moves 3-star rates by 13-40 points (careful-pol 80-100% vs careful 56-67%). Buying the policy also removes the rush lesson for that player: careful-pol faces a triage turn in only 20-26% of HD/CY/FS/BA story runs, against 69-84% for careful. The coach tip invites the buy ('or buy the Policy?'). This goes against the owner's 'one decision per screen / a lot at once' rule. The story at T2 policy was rejected as 'too easy' only on the perfect-reader bot: director dir-t2 shows human80 at 39.8% in CN/BA.

P9: The display shuffle adds a lot of risk for one job. The job is beating a 'mark the last line' guess (86 of 133 proof rows are still last). The costs: it breaks authored reading order for ESL readers and future Ticket/Record pairs (2b 'side'); keyboard focus (rover) must follow display order while marks stay content-indexed (EvidencePanel.tsx:193,218,525-532), and screen readers read the shuffled order; it adds golden churn and B6. A one-time content reorder plus a position lint does the same job with no runtime code. Shuffle does not stop replay memorization, because proof is judged by label, not position.

P10: Stage 2a is not one pass. It has 10 work items across 6 builders plus an integrator, 5 new encounter rules, 5 layouts, gen-2 dailies, the proof engine, mastery, UI chips, shuffle, toasts, coach copy, a 133-plan content script, 5 golden recaptures, a balance-test rewrite and B1-B6. It also changes practice evidence flags (G5, script covers practice) while the owner is phone-testing Phase 1a practice, which muddies that feedback. endTurn(marks) for 'Show me' after a reload is scope creep.

P11: Accessibility gaps. There is no e2e for keyboard marking or the screen-reader announcement under the new label-based clue. Nothing checks reduced motion for the new toasts. The 'Show me' button inside an in-turn toast adds a second decision in the middle of a turn. 'Look only' can read to an ESL player as an instruction ('only look'); 'Read only' is the job-ready IT term.
